paper.title: Stochastic Reset Pathfinding: Path-Level Regret for Cascading Bandits over Graph Paths

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Reset Pathfinding (SRP) / combinatorial cascading bandit over source-to-goal paths
unmapped: Conjunctive (product) reward: path reward is the product of Bernoulli edge outcomes; expected reward prod_e p_e
Feedback: edge outcomes observed sequentially up to and including the first failure along the path
Edge probabilities p_e in [p_min, 1) with p_min > 0 a known constant (the learner knows p_min, used for clipping)
Known directed graph with known source and goal; actions are simple source-to-goal paths
settings.definition_quote: An \srp{} environment is a tuple $(G, v_s, v_g, \mathcal{P})$ where $G = (V, E)$ is a known directed graph, $v_s \ne v_g \in V$ are known source and goal nodes, and $\mathcal{P} = (p_e)_{e \in E} \in [0,1]^{|E|}$ is a vector of stationary edge success probabilities unknown to the agent. ... There exists a known constant $p_{\min} > 0$ such that $p_e \in [p_{\min}, 1)$ for all $e \in E$.

symbols.C_pi: path complexity C(pi) = sum_i S_i(pi)/sqrt(Q_i(pi)) of suboptimal path pi
symbols.Q_L_pi: prefix reliability of the last edge of pi, prod_{j<L} p_{e_j}
symbols.p_min: known lower bound on edge success probabilities

conditions: p_e in [p_min, 1) for all edges with known p_min > 0 (Assumption 1)

source.label: thm:path_dependent_regret
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assum:strict_bounds} with $\rho \ge 2$, the expected cumulative regret of \optinll{} satisfies \mathbb{E}[R(T)] \le \sum_{\pi \notin \Psi^*} \frac{8\rho\,C(\pi)^2\,\ln T}{\Delta(\pi)} + \sum_{\pi \notin \Psi^*} \frac{24\,\ln T}{Q_L(\pi)} + O\!\left(|E| + \frac{|\Psi(v_s,v_g)|\,L_{\max}}{T}\right).

results.notes: Sums are over suboptimal paths (the 'arms'), encoded with sum_subopt. The leading terms carry explicit constants, but the whole bound is recorded under O because of the O(.) remainder. Regret is defined via path reliabilities, so it is pseudo-regret. PathUCB is horizon-free (Remark 3), so the result is anytime, although Algorithm 1 lists T as the loop length.

cited_results.setting_description: Combinatorial cascading bandit with conjunctive reward, here applied to SRP with feasible set of source-to-goal paths; edge-level gap-dependent bound
Combinatorial semi-bandit with multiplicative (conjunctive) reward; lower bound on the leading regret constant of TS, where k* is the size of the optimal solution
